text:
UTA and PIT meet again ten days after Utah's 5-4 win, a game our numbers say the Mammoth deserved to win 75% of the time. Both teams are 2-3-0 in their last five. Utah comes in off a 3-1 home loss to Minnesota, with John Marino and Michael Carcone out. Pittsburgh, rested since an overtime win over Nashville on Oct. 24 (Ville Koivunen scored the winner), is without Bryan Rust. With Rust out, Tommy Novak has moved in beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell and is up to 18:04 a night from 14:05.

Utah has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, Pittsburgh 54%, so there's little between them there. Utah has also taken 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. In net, projected starter Sebastian Cossa (UTA) is at -2.5 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's stopped compared with what an average goalie would). Arturs Silovs (PIT), also projected, is at +1.5, though he was at -12.8 last season.

For Utah, we like Dylan Guenther at 37% to score; he scored on the power play Oct. 25 and was drafted ninth overall in 2021. Pittsburgh's Rakell is at 30% and Crosby at 29%. Novak is one assist from 100 for his career. Our under-the-radar pick is Anders Lee, a third-line Utah forward at about 13 minutes a night, with 3.8 expected goals in his last 10 games. We have him at 22% to score, a player to watch.
